1.why: In /api/verify-token the token record's sessionId must equal the current session id (token.sessionId !== session.id fails), so the code is bound to the requester who asked for it.

2.why: A reset code cannot be used by anyone else because verification rejects tokens whose stored sessionId does not match the caller's session cookie, and tokens are single-use.

3.why: There is no session-invalidation/rotation logic after /api/reset-password — the session object is merely updated in place and other sessions in the `sessions` map are untouched, so prior sessions would remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key plus HSTS and an HTTP→HTTPS 308 redirect, though no explicit minimum TLS version is set (it relies on Bun defaults, which negotiate TLS 1.3).

5.why: Reset tokens are generated with randomBytes(32) and stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10), although the MFA code is kept in plaintext in the session.

6.why: No email is ever sent; the 'recovery message' is simulated by returning mockToken in the JSON response and printing the code and verification link into the page's log pane and browser console, which does not guard the secret.

7.why: Identifiers, tokens, MFA codes and passwords are all validated against strict regexes/length and policy checks, and all dynamic output is written via textContent.

8.why: The only redirect is a fixed 308 to https://localhost:PORT/, and the simulated verification link is a same-origin relative '/verify?token=' with encodeURIComponent — no user-controlled redirect targets exist.

9.why: There are no email templates at all in the code, so the claim cannot be verified positively, though the equivalent HTML rendering path injects no user input and uses a nonce-based CSP.

10.why: Reset tokens and the MFA code are deliberately written to the browser console and the visible <pre id="logs"> element (mockLog("Mock reset delivery: recovery code " + result.mockToken)), so secrets do appear in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and never persisted in plaintext, but the security code is hardcoded in the source as MOCK_MFA_CODE = "482916".

12.why: The hardcoded constant MFA code "482916" is effectively a default credential that always satisfies /api/verify-mfa for any session.

13.why: Source-address-hashed, server-wide expiring counters cap recovery requests at 3 and token/MFA verification failures at 5 per 10-minute window, returning 429 thereafter.

14.why: /api/recovery-request always returns the same generic message ("If the details match an account, a recovery message has been prepared.") regardless of the identifier supplied.

15.why: The reset code is randomBytes(32) encoded base64url, stored hashed with a 10-minute TTL, single-use, and bound to the requesting session.
